title: Mueller residents upset after self-driving car runs over, kills duck

reading.body:
A self-driving car operated by Avride struck and killed a duck in Austin, Texas, while operating in autonomous mode with a human safety operator present. The vehicle did not avoid or stop for the animal. This shows a gap in what the autonomous system was built to detect and respond to, or how its training data prepared it for small animals in its path.

The incident occurred during actual deployment in a neighborhood, not in controlled testing. A human safety operator was present but did not intervene before impact. It is not established whether the operator could have prevented the collision or what the system's detection capabilities are for small animals in real-world conditions.

The company subsequently restricted operations in the area and stated it is evaluating technology improvements. Residents also alleged the vehicle failed to stop at a stop sign, but Avride disputed this after reviewing vehicle data, so it is not established whether this secondary failure occurred.

reports.title: A self-driving car in Texas hit and killed a mother duck, sparking neighborhood outrage
Residents say self-driving car killed duck in Mueller
Self-driving car runs over Mueller Lake Park duck, raising safety concerns
Mueller residents upset after self-driving car runs over, kills duck

summary:
An autonomous vehicle operated by Avride struck and killed a mother duck in the Mueller Lake neighborhood of Austin, Texas, generating significant neighborhood anger. The self-driving car, which had a human safety operator present, did not stop after hitting the duck that residents knew well, as it had been nesting in a pot outside a local restaurant. Local residents posted about the incident on a neighborhood Facebook group, and media coverage followed. Avride confirmed the vehicle was operating in autonomous mode at the time. Residents also alleged the vehicle failed to stop at a stop sign, though Avride disputed this claim after reviewing vehicle data.

In response to the incident, Avride has excluded certain streets around the lake from its testing operations. The company stated it is now evaluating improvements to its autonomous vehicle technology to help prevent similar situations. Avride emphasized that it reviewed multiple replays of the incident in simulation and plans controlled experiments to ensure any changes do not compromise safety in other scenarios. The duck's eggs were rescued by residents and placed in an incubator. Other companies, including Waymo, Tesla, and Zoox, continue testing or operating autonomous vehicles in Austin.
